rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

agent.problem: The phrase "this kind of sexual immorality" points back to card 1, which is no longer visible. The question itself does not explain that a man in the Corinthian church has his father's wife.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: Nothing in the opening card gives the baker a basis for choosing "pagans" over "soldiers" or "priests." The blank asks for an unseen word from the verse rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: By explaining that Paul was not including immoral or greedy people "of this world," this card rules out both wrong answers on card 4: people outside the church and people in Corinth who have never heard of Jesus. That leaves the correct answer before verse 11 is introduced.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
